prompt:
Let X be a geometric random variable with parameter p. Then, for
any two positive integers m, n with m > n, find P (X ≤ m|X ≥ n)
judge_reasoning: The correct conditional probability for a geometric random variable (support {1,2,...}) is P(X≤m|X≥n)=P(n≤X≤m)/P(X≥n), which simplifies to 1−(1−p)^{m−n+1}. Candidate 1 sets up the conditional probability correctly as a ratio of the appropriate sums (even though it doesn’t fully simplify). Candidates 2, 3, and 4 do not compute the requested conditional probability: they answer different questions or drift to unrelated material (expected value, Poisson comparison, and an unconditional CDF respectively).
